review_mode: read-only; metadata, reports, recipes and source inspection only
question: Which historical plain-GRU recipe knowledge can responsibly inform the revised eight-L4 GALAM quality screen and a possible clean GRU teacher?

protocol.primary: official earlier train membership for fitting, complete later official valid for evaluation, whole sequences, fitting-only normalization and ancestry
protocol.historical_status: Existing random-fold F0/F1/F3 results remain exposed historical development evidence. They are not retrospective chronological confirmation; seq_ix is not time.

findings.finding: The recurrent scores most useful for architecture and optimizer priors came from random/component fold panels, including the repeatedly inspected F0 468-group panel and historical F1/F3 panels. ADR0044 now requires the official train-to-full-valid file boundary. These historical scores cannot rank new recipes on the required primary endpoint or establish a time-transfer effect.

findings.consequence: Treat every historical score below as a recipe prior only. Use the official train and full official valid membership for the new primary comparison; do not derive another split order from seq_ix.

findings.finding: The closest historical scratch recipe to a strong plain-GRU starting point is H256x2 with 211 causal inputs, batch 32, chunk 1000, three epochs, LR 1e-3, recurrent-matrix Muon, OneCycle (the run receipt records sched=onecycle; profile_warmup=5 is a profiling field, and the scheduler warmup fraction is not bound by the inspected provenance), FP16, clipped |y|-weighted MSE and aux_next=0.3 plus aux_struct=0.3. Its provenance binds train_source=train+valid and a random fold-0 split; it also uses a fold-specific propensity model. The run is not a clean precedent for current chronological fitting.

findings.consequence: This bundle is the best-supported historical plain-GRU hyperparameter prior found, not a measured ideal and not an exact recipe to reuse. A prospective model must start fresh, recompute all transforms on official train only, exclude valid-derived mask/propensity/teacher/initializer ancestry, and report any precision or feature change as an adaptation.

findings.finding: The historical H256x2 warm lineage reached 0.68282334 for its parent and 0.68314181 for the two-epoch student, but the student-parent delta is only about +0.000318 and its paired component interval [-0.001320, +0.001799] crosses zero. The student used a different alpha=0.7 teacher/cache, LR=1e-4, FP16 and B16/C1000 continuation. The parent provenance uses train+valid and a family teacher cache. This cannot be presented as a fresh scratch-GRU win or a teacher-transfer effect.

findings.finding: On the short exposed F0 teacher-target screen, H512x1 beat H256x2 by +0.00346012 (conditional component-bootstrap 95% interval [+0.00200307,+0.00490448]); H384x2 beat it by +0.0019104 (interval [+0.0003020,+0.0034776]). H256x1 was effectively tied, while H192x2 was lower. On a separate cold labels-only F3 comparison, H512x1 and H384x2 were essentially tied: deep-minus-wide +0.0001154, interval [-0.0024723,+0.0020551]. These are distinct one-seed recipes/folds, and the bootstrap is conditional on fixed predictions.

findings.consequence: No universal width/depth winner follows. In particular, the historical H384 contrast is not a +0.0012 robust chronological result. H512x1 is a useful candidate, not a default theorem; these dimensions do not map directly to GALAM width.

findings.finding: The best-aligned historical main objective is squared error on labels/predictions clipped at +/-2 with row mass proportional to abs(clipped label), matching the global metric's clipping and target weighting. Historical stronger variants add propensity weights, true-mask weighting, auxiliary objectives and validation-row fine-tuning. Official train lacks is_scored, and the old mask/propensity pipeline used exposed validation-side information. Current GALAM v1 configs use all post-warmup train rows, train-only normalization and no teacher/propensity/auxiliary cache.

findings.consequence: Retain clipped |y|-weighted MSE as the simple supervised prior. Do not import a valid-derived propensity model, true-mask fitting, validation LP-FT, or old teacher caches. Any train-only propensity/auxiliary extension is a separate fitted recipe whose ancestry and incremental effect must be recorded.

findings.finding: Muon-RNN with LR 1e-3/OneCycle is a documented historical recipe, but no isolated chronological comparison establishes it as the best for GALAM. A historical F1 effects screen reports AdamW switch delta -0.00411 with interval [-0.00935,+0.00113], LR=5e-4 delta -0.00217 with interval [-0.00559,+0.00125], and Muon LR multiplier 6 delta -0.00550 with interval [-0.00955,-0.00145]. This was a single old fold/seed screen with many attempted variants. Legacy src/wnn/optim.py supports recurrent Muon groups; the new sequence optimizer is Transformer-specific and sequence_config.py rejects GALAM+Muon.
evidence: artifacts/runs/combo_scratch_f0ep3s3_onecycle_f0/provenance.json: Muon RNN LR=1e-3 scratch bundle.
hpo/evidence/scratch_effects_fold1.json: one-fold effect estimates and component intervals.

src/wnn/training/sequence_optimizer.py and src/wnn/training/sequence_config.py: current sequence Muon is Transformer-only; GALAM v1 requires FP32 AdamW.
findings.consequence: For the current GALAM panel, use one supported optimizer and schedule across all eight arms. Do not apply Muon to A3 only. A GRU Muon comparison or a GALAM hybrid optimizer requires an explicit implementation/config amendment and a matched control; neither has present GALAM quality evidence.

findings.finding: The project history warns that longer fitting on this label-noise-dominated task can degrade validation: the 2026-09-28 synthesis says 8+ epochs without EMA memorized noise, and the F1 effects screen reports six epochs at -0.01739 (interval [-0.03018,-0.00460]) and an eight-epoch Muon/EMA variant at -0.03623 (interval [-0.05286,-0.01960]) versus its local baseline. These are old, non-chronological and recipe-specific negatives; they do not prove that a correctly retimed 20-epoch GALAM run will fail. The common-20-epoch proposal is unmaterialized; an early epoch on a 20-epoch cosine schedule is not the same recipe as a standalone five-epoch run.
evidence: research/brief-2026-09-28-optim.md: overfit warning for 8+ epochs without EMA.

findings.consequence: The user-accepted 20-epoch concept can be carried forward as a deliberate common schedule amendment, not as a historically discovered optimum. Freeze one schedule across arms, report fixed common epoch 5/10/20 checkpoints, and do not equate the epoch-5 checkpoint with a separate five-epoch run. Treat valid-selected checkpoints as exposed development selections.

findings.finding: The current A3 is the schematic GALAM GRU72 variant (112 inputs to two outputs, about 358,170 parameters) versus the GALAM LSTM64 baseline (about 376,426). It retains the global/local attention/mixer/fusion design while changing recurrence type and width. Historical plain GRUs use a 211-feature encoder with different heads, objectives and training ancestry. GALAM's original source code, checkpoint and complete hyperparameters are unavailable; the reconstruction is explicitly schematic, not exact.

clean_retraining_rules: new random initialization and new run identity
fit only on official train sequences; no valid rows in normalization, propensity, teacher, initializer, or optimizer state ancestry
full official valid is evaluation only; never valid LP-FT or true-mask training
recompute sampler/update totals and schedule from actual train membership

It would change the architecture and optimization treatment together. If selected as a separate clean teacher, declare the additional/substituted fit and ancestry explicitly.

current_galam_comparison.common_control: Preserve the current supported AdamW/FP32/common-loss/common-schedule recipe across every arm unless a formal v2 amendment changes all arms together.
current_galam_comparison.A3_interpretation: Keep the schematic GRU72 arm as an architecture comparison, not a known best preset.
current_galam_comparison.20_epoch_revision: May be adopted as an explicit shared schedule amendment, with a retimed schedule and fixed checkpoints at common epochs; historical evidence does not nominate 20 as optimal.
current_galam_comparison.selection: Use the official full-valid metric each epoch as exposed development reporting. Predeclare any best-valid checkpoint rule and describe its result as validation-selected; do not call it independent confirmation.
